Hi Lisa —

Thanks — appreciate the timeline. I've attached a short RFI response pack that addresses TAM coverage, escalation tiers, and our incident comms template (see attachments: Redwood_TAM_RFI_Responses.pdf, SLA-Escalation-Path.pdf). High-level summary below — I can arrange a 30-minute walkthrough later this week with Grace (TAM lead) and Marissa (Support Ops) if you'd like a live review.

High-level:
- TAM coverage: dedicated TAM + pooled after-hours on-call. Named TAM available for enterprise contracts; 24x7 incident escalation via on-call rotations for Severity 1.
- Response SLAs (target):
  - Sev1: initial response within 15 minutes, continuous engagement until mitigation
  - Sev2: initial response within 1 hour
  - Sev3: next-business-hour acknowledgement; resolution SLAs vary by scope
- Incident comms: immediate PagerDuty/SMS + primary channel in Slack/Teams; formal incident report within 48 hours; root cause and postmortem within 10 business days by default.

I'll leave Grace and Marissa on copy to provide the more detailed coverage matrix you asked for (hours, escalation contacts, runbook handoff).

Best,

Hi Lisa —

Following up with the detailed coverage notes Karthik promised. I've attached a coverage matrix (TAM_Coverage_Matrix_v1.xlsx) and included answers inline for your procurement and platform teams.

Summary (short version):
- Designated TAM model: For enterprise contracts we provide a named TAM (primary) plus a secondary TAM. The named TAM is accountable for weekly check-ins, runbook delivery, and escalation coordination.
- Coverage hours: Named TAM (Mon–Fri, 9am–5pm local PT) with engineering-backed 24x7 on-call for Severity 1 incidents via our SRE escalation bridge.
- On-call rotation & hand-off: TAMs operate on a regional named basis; SRE on-call is global and rotates every 7 days. Handoffs are coordinated via a shared runbook and a 30-minute overlap during shift changes for critical accounts.
- Escalation tiers (short):
  1. Tier 1: Redwood Support (CS engineer) — first triage, initial mitigation (Sev3/Sev2).
  2. Tier 2: TAM + Technical SME — deeper debugging, coordinate engineering resources (Sev2/Sev1).
  3. Tier 3: SRE/Platform Eng & Director on-call — full incident bridge and customer exec comms (Sev1).
- Response SLAs (target operating targets):
  - Sev1: 15 minutes to acknowledge, 30 minutes to initial mitigation update, continuous bridge until containment.
  - Sev2: 1 hour to acknowledge, 4 hours to mitigation plan.
  - Sev3: 4 business hours to acknowledge.
- Incident communications:
  - Immediate: PagerDuty + SMS + direct Slack channel for engineering engagement.
  - T+2 hours: Incident update to primary contacts.
  - T+48 hours: Preliminary incident report with timeline and short-term mitigations.
  - T+10 business days: RCA and postmortem with action items.
- Optional add-ons: Extended TAM hours (overnight coverage), dedicated 24x7 engineering retainer (additional fee), anonymized weekly incident trend reports (add-on).

Exceptions & Notes:
- Blackout periods: Any scheduled maintenance windows agreed to in the contract are excluded from Sev1/Sev2 billing adjustments.
- Holidays: Coverage follows customer region holidays for named-TAM weekly check-ins; global SRE on-call unaffected.

Attachments included: TAM_Coverage_Matrix_v1.xlsx (single sheet: hours/contacts/SLA table) and the SLA-Escalation-Path.pdf previously sent. If you'd like, Marissa can create a one-page diagram for inclusion in your RFP appendix.

Would you like a 30-minute call on Thursday to walk through the matrix with Karthik, Marissa, and me?

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Principal TAM, Redwood Inference
